audit.whatIsWrong: The core survival instruction for levels 1-2 is to hide behind the wave: 'stand behind minions and never let him land Q' (spikes[0]), 'Stand behind your minions constantly: Rupture's ground indicator cannot reach you through a wave' (early), 'stand behind minions and give no angle for Q to land' (whys[0]).
audit.why: Rupture is a ground-targeted area effect cast at a location up to 950 units away — it is not a projectile and minions do not block, absorb or shorten it. Standing behind the wave gives a Teemo exactly zero protection from the one ability the entry calls lethal, while also keeping him inside its range. The only counterplay to Rupture is movement during its wind-up. This is the most dangerous line in the matchup because it converts correct fear into a defensive habit that does not work.
audit.corrected: Rupture is a location-targeted zone, 950 range, with a wind-up. Minions do not block it — you dodge it by moving, and by staying beyond 950 when you can.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json — Q Rupture: 'Ruptures the ground at target location', range 950, no projectile flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Rupture's cooldown is given as 9 seconds twice — 'trade on his Rupture cooldown (around 9 seconds early)' in early, and 'you have a full 9-second window to pour poison into him freely' in mid. The packet also flags this matchup as having no cooldown-sequencing advice.
audit.why: Rupture is 6 seconds flat at every rank. The entry overstates Teemo's safe window by 50%, and it errs in the fatal direction: a player who commits to a three-second poke loop believing he has nine seconds before the next knockup gets caught by the one ability that starts Cho'Gath's kill combo. Correcting it also finally supplies the sequencing the packet asked for, because the real numbers are clean — Rupture 6s flat, Feral Scream 11s at rank 1, Vorpal Spikes 8s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rupture 6s flat at all ranks. Feral Scream 11/10.5/10/9.5/9. Vorpal Spikes 8/7/6/5/4. Wait for Rupture to be spent, then you have six seconds — not nine.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feast is described as gaining reach and damage from stacks: 'Feast stacks give Cho'Gath true-damage execute range' (spikes[3]), 'his R true-damage one-shot range grows with every Feast stack' (late), 'a true-damage execute (R) that deletes you from range' (whys[6]), 'Stack Feast (R) to 6 for massive HP and execute range' (wants.foe[1]).
audit.why: Feast stacks grant maximum Health and nothing else — the ability's damage does not scale with them, and its range is a fixed 175, which is closer than Cho'Gath's own auto-attack. It cannot delete anyone 'from range'. The practical consequence is the reverse of what the entry implies: a stacked Cho'Gath is harder to kill, not longer-armed, and a Teemo who stays outside 175 units simply cannot be Feasted no matter how many stacks are on the bar.
audit.corrected: Feast: 175 range, 80/70/60s, high flat true damage. Stacks give max Health only — not damage, not range. Stay outside 175 and it cannot touch you.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json — R Feast: 'Devours an enemy unit, dealing a high amount of true damage. If the target is killed, Cho'Gath grows, gaining maximum Health.', range 175, cooldown 80/70/60

audit.whatIsWrong: Vorpal Spikes is never mentioned in either layer, and the blind is justified only as cancelling generic 'autos'.
audit.why: Vorpal Spikes rides on Cho'Gath's basic attacks — they release spikes that damage and slow everything in front of him. That makes Blinding Dart far better here than the entry claims: a blinded attack lands nothing, so it denies the spike damage AND the slow, and the slow is the only reason a Teemo who respects Rupture range ever gets caught. Blinding the attack is how you keep your kiting intact, not just how you shave damage.
audit.corrected: Vorpal Spikes rides his basic attacks and slows. Blind the attack and you deny both the damage and the slow that lets him close.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json — E Vorpal Spikes: 'Cho'Gath's attacks release deadly spikes, dealing damage and slowing all enemy units in front of him', flags slow

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream is treated as a general threat with no range given — 'W back before Feral Scream range' is as specific as it gets.
audit.why: Feral Scream is a 300-range cone. Teemo auto-attacks at 500 and Blinding Dart reaches 680, so the entire silence threat lives inside a band Teemo never has to enter. Naming the number converts a vague 'respect his pattern' into a hard positional rule the player can hold all lane.
audit.corrected: Feral Scream is a 300-range cone. Your auto is 500 and Blinding Dart is 680 — poke from outside 300 and the silence simply cannot reach you.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json — Q Blinding Dart range 680, E Toxic Shot range 680

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Blinding Shot' is used instead of Blinding Dart in spikes[0], spikes[1], early, mid, whys[1], whys[2] and whys[4].
audit.why: Wrong name for the player's own primary ability, repeated seven times in one matchup.
Liandry's Torment is named correctly here — the only matchup in my slice where the item spelling is already right — and the percent-health-versus-Feast-stacks logic is sound. No change.

edits.before: Level 1 and 2 are the danger window — Cho'Gath's Rupture knockup is telegraphed but lethal if it connects, and Feral Scream silence stops you from blinding him out of the follow-up auto burst. Stand behind your minions constantly: Rupture's ground indicator cannot reach you through a wave, and you can freely poison him from max E range while he farms. Never auto-walk toward him at Level 1 fishing for a trade — if Rupture clips you, you die or burn Flash. Once you hit Level 2 and have Blinding Shot available, you can trade on his Rupture cooldown (around 9 seconds early), but only if you are certain Rupture is down and you have W ready to escape his Feral Scream silence window.
edits.after: Level 1 and 2 are the danger window — Rupture is telegraphed but lethal if it connects, and Feral Scream's silence stops you blinding your way out of the follow-up. Do not stand behind minions expecting cover: Rupture is a ground-targeted zone at 950 range and the wave does not block it, so you dodge by moving during the wind-up. Feral Scream is only a 300-range cone, though, so poison him from 680 and the silence never reaches you. Never walk at him at Level 1 fishing for a trade. From Level 2, trade on his Rupture cooldown — 6 seconds flat, not nine — but only with Rupture confirmed spent and W held ready for the exit.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where this lane swings your way — Blinding Shot has meaningful CDR from Transcendence, your E poison is ticking constantly, and every bush in the lane is a mushroom landmine he must acknowledge. The pattern is simple: auto-poke on every CS he walks up to last-hit, Q-blind the moment he raises his auto animation, and W back before Feral Scream range. If he burns Rupture to try to catch you, you have a full 9-second window to pour poison into him freely. At Level 6 his Feast becomes relevant — a 6-stack Cho'Gath has a massive HP pool that your DoT cannot race in a short trade — so accelerate the Liandry's spike rather than trying to burst him down before he scales.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where this lane swings your way — your E poison ticks constantly and every bush is a mushroom landmine he must acknowledge. The pattern is simple: auto-poke on every CS he walks up to last-hit, Blinding Dart the moment he winds up an attack so Vorpal Spikes deals no damage and lands no slow, and W back before you enter Feral Scream's 300-range cone. If he burns Rupture chasing you, that is a 6-second window — real, but shorter than it feels, so poison and reposition rather than overstaying. At Level 6 Feast gives him a max-Health pool your DoT cannot race in a short trade, so accelerate Liandry's rather than trying to burst him.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment is the matchup-winning purchase: the percent-health burn on your poison stacks and mushrooms directly counter his Feast HP stacks, turning every shroom he walks into a disproportionate chunk of his health bar. At 2+ items Cho'Gath becomes a genuine execution threat — his R true-damage one-shot range grows with every Feast stack, meaning a single Rupture-Scream combo into R deletes you at half HP. Your winning play is never the extended 1v1 in the late game: plant your mushrooms on every path into sidelane objectives, split from safety behind your shroom net, and force him to choose between wasting Feast on creeps or walking into a mushroom field to find you.
edits.after: Liandry's Torment is the matchup-winning purchase: percent-health burn on your poison and mushrooms counters his Feast Health stacks directly, turning every shroom he walks into a disproportionate chunk of his bar. At 2+ items he is a genuine execution threat, but be precise about why: Feast is fixed at 175 range and its damage does not grow with stacks — what grows is the Health he brings to reach you. A Rupture-Scream combo into melee is the death sentence, not the R itself. Plant mushrooms on every path into sidelane objectives, split behind the net, and force him to choose between Feasting creeps or walking into a minefield.

notes: The packet's 'no cooldown-sequencing advice' flag was half right — there were two sequencing lines, but both used a 9-second Rupture cooldown when it is 6 seconds flat at every rank, so the advice was worse than none. The bigger problem was the standing-behind-minions instruction, repeated three times as the level 1-2 survival plan: Rupture is a location-targeted ground zone, not a projectile, and the wave gives no protection whatsoever from it. I also corrected the Feast description, which had stacks granting execute damage and range when they grant maximum Health only — Feast is a fixed 175 range, shorter than Cho'Gath's own auto-attack, which is a far more useful thing for a kiting champion to know. Added the two range numbers that make the lane mechanical rather than vibes-based: Feral Scream is a 300 cone against Teemo's 680 poke range, and Vorpal Spikes rides his basic attacks so the blind denies its slow as well as its damage. Kit-file caveat: chogath.json tags Rupture with a 'grounding' flag, which appears to be derived from the words 'Ruptures the ground' rather than from any grounding effect — Riot's text describes a knockup and a slow only, so I asserted nothing about grounding. The single flagged suspect name, 'Blinding Shot', was genuine and appears seven times in this matchup; my edits fix it in five of them, with the remaining two inside strings I had no other reason to rewrite.
